msDesc.head: The ‘Martindale Leaves’, fragments of a St Albans Psalter, 13th century, first quarter

msItem.title: Psalter
msItem.note: Three bifolia containing parts of the canticles, creed, litany, collects, and of the Office of the Dead. Other leaves from the same manuscript are Toronto, Massey College Library, Robertson Davies Rare Book Collections, MS Gurney Pam 0008; and another leaf was sold at Bloomsbury Auctions, 10 October 2008, lot 5.

listBibl.bibl: Michael A. Michael, ‘The Martindale and Gurney Leaves: A Dismembered Early Thirteenth-Century Psalter from St Albans Abbey Reunited’, The Bodleian Library Record, 38.1–2 (2025), pp. 36–63, doi:10.3828/blr.2025.38.1-2.36

layoutDesc.layout: 24 long lines, written above top line, ruled in green and red ink, ruled space 223 194

handDesc.handNote: Formal textualis (semi-precissa). Probably written by the same scribe as BL Royal MS 13 D V (Geoffrey of Monmouth; St Albans, after 1206 and before c. 1235).

decoDesc.decoNote: Initials on gold ground with penwork flourishing.

history.provenance: St Albans Abbey: liturgical evidence, and evidence of script

Note dated 1582, fol. 2v: '4 Novemb 82 his presentibus Stephano Cpp Gulielmo Raynes in Hoving'. The fifteen known surviving leaves of the psalter perhaps 'were once sewn together to create one large sheet that was possibly used as a lining for a wooden object at some point after 1582. This was rediscovered, disassembled and sold as fragments before 1974.' (A. Honey, 'Bodleian Library, MS. Lat. Liturg. d. 48, The Martindale Leaves - Conservation Report', 2026 https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:cae9b319-524f-4ea3-8408-c45a3cb357eb)
Andrew Martindale (1932-1995), historian of art, acquired in the 1970s; his wife, Jane Martindale (-2023)
history.acquisition: Given to the Bodleian on their behalf by Michael Michael in 2025 with the request that the fragments be known as the 'Martindale leaves'.
